page: Google Cloud Platform n4d-standard-4 is a general-purpose server instance featuring 4 vCPUs and 16 GB of RAM, powered by an AMD EPYC 9B45 processor. This x86_64 architecture configuration provides 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core under a dedicated CPU allocation model. The processor includes 48 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, including VNNI and BF16, and cryptography standards like AES and SHA_NI. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier single-core CPU capabilities, with stress-ng single-core performance and Geekbench single-core scores ranking in the top 10%. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also achieve top-tier results. However, multi-core scaling is more moderate, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores falling into the average category. A notable bottleneck is the uncached large-block memory read bandwidth, which registers in the bottom 25% at 37.73 GB/sec, contrasted with a robust cached small-block read bandwidth of 418.9 GB/sec. Database operations also show weakness, placing in the bottom 25% on PassMark benchmarks.

From a resource density perspective, the n4d-standard-4 offers a balanced vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 1:4, making it a cost-efficient option for workloads that benefit from strong single-thread execution without requiring massive memory footprints or local storage. It is aligned with general-purpose workloads, static web serving, text processing, and lightweight single-threaded data compression tasks. It is less appropriate for memory-intensive database systems or heavy multi-threaded compute tasks due to its memory bandwidth limitations and average multi-core performance.
